That is not what it is talking about. Micah shows what the wine is.

“If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” The wine and strong drink are the falsehoods and the lies. It is not the priests and prophets actually getting drunk and teaching; it is them pushing doctrines.

Read Isaiah again with that: they have erred through doctrine, lies and falsehoods, and are out of the way of the Lord. “they err in vision, they stumble in judgment”: they do not teach correctly; it is their erroneous doctrine. “For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.”

precepts.text: For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope, and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.
precepts.point: His God doth instruct him to discretion. Discreet means careful and circumspect in speech or action, to avoid causing offence or to gain an advantage. Learn discernment: how to speak and when to speak, which someone should tell our wives, in order to win souls.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Isaiah gives an analogy of a farmer: “Doth the plowman plow all day to sow? doth he open and break the clods of his ground?” He breaks the dirt, makes the ground flat, and casts abroad his seeds. But is Isaiah really talking about farmland?

Paul answers it: “Or saith he it altogether for our sakes? For our sakes, no doubt, this is written: that he that ploweth should plow in hope; and that he that thresheth in hope should be partaker of his hope.” It wasn't really talking about farms. The plowing and the threshing were not about growing seeds.

The plowing represents teaching. We are to plow in hope: to teach, instruct, and give hope to our people. You brothers are fishers of men, and the field is our people. That is how Isaiah 28 applies to you.

So the fitches, cummin, principal wheat, appointed barley and rye are the different people we plow for, and the farmer's instruments are the different ways we must deal with them to persuade them to salvation. By long forbearing even a prince is persuaded, and Israel is a prince: we have to be patient with our people.

Sometimes the brother will not come in because you spoke out of season while he was stressed from work and his mind was closed. You know how to speak, and you know when to speak.

You may say, I'm putting my time in teaching this brother and he won't come to the school. Read this: “To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven”. Not to some things, not to little things: to every thing there is a season.

So when we're fishing, there is a time to talk about the truth with that brother. Sometimes you're talking out of season. He was stressed from work, things were going on, his mind just wasn't open, and you didn't discern it. But if you pay attention and watch, the moment comes: Leroy calls and says, I was watching this documentary about the space landing, and I'm starting to think this world isn't what I thought it was. Got him. You waited two years for Leroy, and Leroy opened up.

At the end of the day the Lord brings them in. But we are at war, Russia and China are about to get involved, and it's only going to get worse. We have to be better fishermen, and be patient with our brothers and sisters.

“But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.” Brothers, you have to know what manner of spirit you're supposed to be in when you deal with the people in the street. Always represent this truth with the utmost professionalism, because we have a job: to win souls, and we don't have much time. precepts.text: They gave me vinegar to drink. Let their table become a snare, and that which should have been for their welfare a trap; let their eyes be darkened, that they see not. Christ speaking through David about the rulers.
precepts.point: Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone. Their covenant with death shall be disannulled. Today that covenant is the Christian pastors and Black politicians in bed with America, as the rulers then were in bed with Rome; and 'the report' they will not understand is Isaiah 53:1, that Christ is Messiah.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the word came to the rulers “that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.” David shows the same snare. “They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.” This is a writing of David, but it is Christ speaking through David regarding himself on the cross.

“Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.” Let the rulers' table be a snare. That is why Isaiah said they would be snared, trapped, broken and stumble.

“Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not”: let the eyes of the elders, the rulers, be darkened, whereunto they were appointed, so that they see not the Messiah standing in front of them. When he walked on the earth they said, that's not the guy, it can't be him. The rest of the verse: “and make their loins continually to shake.”

So the prophecy of Isaiah 28 is in reference to the elders, the leaders that ruled us. They hated God and they hated their people, and the words of God through the prophets were darkened to them.

They stumbled, fell and were broken, as Psalm 69 said, and rejected the Messiah because they were evil, sinful and rebellious. That is who he is talking to: the elders, the builders, the rulers.

Not all Israel refused him; the builders refused him. Appointed means they were predestined to reject him. Take good notes and tie these together: Isaiah 28, Isaiah 8, Psalm 118 and 1 Peter 2 are the same stone.

precepts.text: I will mar the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem, this evil people which refuse to hear my words and walk in the imagination of their heart, good for nothing as the girdle. precepts.point: It goes back to Rehoboam, who mocked the elders' counsel and listened to his friends, splitting the kingdom; we are in this condition today because of that pride.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Every kingdom on earth has failed because of pride, even ours. Isaiah says “Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim”: the northern kingdom fell because of pride. They separated from God, went to the north and said, we are doing our own thing. It goes back to the split between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Rehoboam could have listened to the elders who were already there to run the nation correctly, but he mocked the leadership above him and dealt with his buddies, and we are in the condition we are in today because of that pride.

The northern kingdom was the first to fall, but the southern kingdom was not exempt. “Thus saith the Lord, After this manner will I mar the pride of Judah, and the great pride of Jerusalem.” Judah looked at what their brother was doing and followed right after their treacherous sister Israel. The great pride of Jerusalem takes in Benjamin and Levi too: all of the southern kingdom was full of pride in God's eyes.

“This evil people, which refuse to hear my words, which walk in the imagination of their heart, and walk after other gods, to serve them, and to worship them, shall even be as this girdle, which is good for nothing.” When pride comes, you separate yourself from your maker, as Sirach 10 says, and walk after your own heart. When you are full of pride you are good for nothing in God's eyes.

Then the judgment for it: “And I will dash them one against another, even the fathers and the sons together, saith the Lord: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have mercy, but destroy them.” Pride destroyed the kingdom, and it destroys every kingdom.

“Hear ye, and give ear; be not proud: for the Lord hath spoken.” You better listen up, Israel, and not separate yourself from him. He is our creator and he controls all of this, so you better humble yourself and do as he tells you. This could be over right now if all of us said, Lord, I'm done with pride, I humble myself, what do you want me to do? And Christ would crack the sky.

But not on the surface, saying forgive me and then waiting till you get out of here. You are not fooling God. That is why we are still here as a people: even those of us that repented are not ready to go back to the kingdom yet. And pride is not always loud. It can be subtle, shutting down, thinking you can do it on your own, and Satan still has you there.
